methods.scalar_statistics: NumPy percentile with default linear interpolation at [0,1,5,25,50,75,95,99,100]; rms=sqrt(mean(values**2)).

length_scale.h: Saved native h. The recorded interior cut is R-2h=.041000000387430194m.

methods.regions: Fixed own-initial material-radius classification, r_initial<R-2h versus r_initial>=R-2h. Old initial/Part50 use old Part0; grad1 uses its own Part0. No reclassification by the deformed radius.
methods.nearest_neighbour: All37173 soil particles: cKDTree(current XYZ).query(current XYZ,k=2), second distance divided by dp. Region membership remains initial-material membership.
methods.local_nonaffinity: For every soil particle take24 fixed nearest neighbours from its own initial geometry. d0=X0_neighbour-X0_i; d=x_neighbour-x_i; A=sum(d0 outer d0), B=sum(d outer d0), F=B inv(A). Report sqrt(mean_neighbours(|d-F d0|^2))/dp. No pressure or time interpolation.
methods.global_affinity: Unweighted least-squares x_current=[X0,1] coef over every soil node. Report coef[:3].T, translation, and norm(x_current-fit)/dp statistics by fixed material region.
methods.local_nonaffinity_limit: This residual also contains physical radial-strain curvature, elastic waves and boundary response. Different physical times are not an isolated option comparison or a pure numerical disorder growth test.
methods.moment_sampling: For each region, available=flatnonzero(region_mask); sample=available[np.linspace(0,len(available)-1,min(512,len(available)),dtype=int)]. Use exactly those initial-ID indices at each snapshot. Regions contain19527 interior/17646 outer native nodes; only512 matrices per region are evaluated, so reported moment maxima are sample maxima, not whole-cloud maxima.
methods.moment_formula: For each sampled receiver query all current soil neighbours r<=2h, omit rr<1e-18. d=x_i-x_j; g=(-2.08891/h**5)*(1-.5*r/h)**3*d. M_i=-sum_j(m_j/rho_j)*d outer g. Uses saved current rho, native mass, double offline arithmetic; not production0ULP. Check all sampled eigenvalues positive.
methods.moment_anisotropy: Condition=lambda_max/lambda_min for symmetric positive M; deviator_norm_over_trace=||M-(trM/3)I||_F/trM. trace_over3 diagnoses moment scale and is not a disorder metric by itself.
methods.cartesian_control: Only an in-memory geometric counterexample: Cartesian nodes ([-20..20]*dp)^3 clipped by sum(x*x)<=R*R+1e-15,33401 nodes, same h/native mass and uniformrho2100. Different N, native volume, and a center node; not GenCase, not a solver input or an admitted replacement distribution.

conclusions: No clear near-neighbour collapse or ill-conditioned moment growth was found at these bounded snapshots. This does not prove all later times remain orderly.
Native initial layout differs from an exact Cartesian lattice and already has non-unit moment scale. Initial geometric/quadrature bias is distinct from time-varying disorder.
The perfectly regular Cartesian control has nearest distances essentially dp but nonidentity/anisotropic outer-shell moments. Support truncation must not be relabelled as particle disorder.

Local residuals remain below.008dp at the two dynamic snapshots and include legitimate non-affine radial physics. Their differing times/options cannot establish which scheme generates more numerical disorder.

These data support continuing existing gradient/force consistency and time-resolution checks before prioritizing online particle shifting. They do not rule out a later controlled layout or state-consistent shifting study.

stock_shifting_source_evidence.finding: Corrector adds ShiftPosfsc XYZ directly to computed displacement and updates position.
GPU corrector likewise adds shiftposfs XYZ to positional displacement.
Symplectic predictor position shift is hardcodedfalse; corrector uses the configured Shifting object.
GPU predictor hardcodes shiftfalse; corrector enables it from ShiftingMode.

Density/velocity and stress/plastic history use their existing rate integration, then retain state at the same particle ID; no displacement-gradient transport/remap appears in this active corrector path.
GPU density/velocity/stress/plastic state likewise retains its existing rate-integrated update, separate from the extra position displacement.
Pore pressure is updated p_pre+dt*p_rate; no shift-state transport term.
GPU pore update is also p_old+dt*p_rate without a shifting remap.
Shift magnitude uses dt*ShiftCoef*h*|v|, scalar ShiftTFS attenuation and per-component0.1dp limits; zero prescribed velocity gives no shifting displacement.
GPU uses the same speed/scalar-threshold/clamping construction.
NoBound/NoFixed refers to actual bound neighbours; the free-surface threshold is accumulated kernel-divergence scalar, not FSType or a normal/tangent position constraint.
Current SPR/HG compatibility guards reject Shifting; HG also requires2D.
GPU SPR/HG guards similarly reject Shifting; do not bypass them.
Generic Shifting parsing supports None/NoBound/NoFixed/Full; no independent Cryer-specific state-transport contract is established here.

stock_shifting_interpretation: For the inspected ordinary CPU/GPU Cryer Symplectic paths, evidence supports position relocation without an accompanying rho/pore/stress/velocity transport/remap. This is not a blanket bug claim about all fluid models, in/out extensions or independent regularizers.

State remains attached to particle ID with physical-rate integration, while position also receives numerical displacement. A material-point settlement or geometry-derived strain diagnostic would need to distinguish accumulated shifting from physical displacement.

Cryer has only a remote dummy boundary, so NoBound/NoFixed does not constrain the free sphere. ShiftTFS can suppress or taper motion but is not a proven sphere-preserving or drainage-preserving constraint.

Relocation could change neighbours, correction matrices, FSType drainage membership and the raw confining-load kernel truncation. Those effects require controlled testing; this audit does not establish that a current solver error was caused by shifting, which remains disabled.
